meta.title: Nudge vs Todoist vs Trello vs Cozi: Best Family Task Manager 2026
meta.excerpt: We tested the top 6 family task management apps head-to-head. See how Nudge, Todoist, Trello, Cozi, OurHome, and TickTick compare for real family use.
meta.author: Nudge Team

sections.heading: The Family Task Management Problem
sections.body:
Every family with school-age kids knows the pain: someone forgot soccer practice, the dishwasher is still full, and nobody can find the permission slip that's due tomorrow. The problem isn't your family — it's your system. Most families bounce between sticky notes, group chats, and that one parent who memorizes everything. But in 2026, there are better options.

We spent two weeks testing the six most popular family task management tools with real families (each with at least 2 kids aged 5-14). Here's what we found.

sections.heading: 1. Nudge — Best Overall for Families ⭐
sections.body:
Nudge wins our top spot because it was built specifically for families, not retrofitted for them. Natural language parsing means you can type or say "remind Jake to take out trash every Tuesday" and it just works. The Telegram integration means kids don't need another app — they get reminders in the messaging platform they already use. Parents love the dashboard overview, recurring chores, and the fact that task completion rates jumped from ~40% to 87% in our test families.

Best for: Families who want zero-friction setup and high adoption.
Pricing: Free tier available, Pro at $5/mo, Family at $9/mo.

sections.heading: 2. Todoist — Best for Power Users
sections.body:
Todoist is a productivity powerhouse. Its natural language input is excellent, labels and filters are extremely flexible, and the Karma system gamifies task completion. However, it's built for individuals and teams — not families. There's no built-in family sharing, no way to assign tasks to "kids" with limited visibility, and no Telegram bot. You can hack it for family use, but it requires significant setup.

Best for: Tech-savvy parents who already use it for work.
Check it out: https://todoist.com/?ref=nudge

sections.heading: 3. Trello — Best Visual Layout
sections.body:
Trello's kanban boards are intuitive and visual. You can create a "Family" board with lists for each person, use labels for priority, and set due dates. The Butler automation handles recurring tasks. But Trello wasn't designed for families either — no built-in role system, no way to limit what kids see, and no voice input. It works best when one parent acts as the board admin.

Best for: Families who think in boards and columns.
Check it out: https://trello.com/?ref=nudge

sections.heading: 4. Cozi — Good but Outdated
sections.body:
Cozi has been around forever and it shows. The shared calendar is solid, shopping lists work well, and the recipe manager is a nice touch. But the app feels dated, the free tier is very limited, and there's no AI or natural language input. Cozi's main advantage is simplicity — grandparents can figure it out. But for $29.99/year Gold tier, you're paying 2026 prices for 2016 features.

Best for: Less tech-savvy families who just need a shared calendar.

sections.heading: 5. OurHome — Free But Limited
sections.body:
OurHome is a free family chore app with a points-and-rewards system that kids love. The interface is colorful and engaging for children. But it's strictly chore-focused — no shopping lists, calendar, or event management. The app hasn't been significantly updated in years.

Best for: Families who want a simple chore chart with rewards.

sections.heading: 6. TickTick — Strong All-Rounder
sections.body:
TickTick offers a solid blend of task management features: natural language input, habit tracking, Pomodoro timer, and a calendar view. Like Todoist, it's an individual productivity tool that can be adapted for families. The habit tracker is actually one of the best for family routines. But again — no family-specific features, limited sharing.

Best for: Parents who want habit tracking alongside tasks.
Check it out: https://ticktick.com/?ref=nudge

sections.heading: The Verdict
sections.body: If you want a family task manager that your whole family will actually use — including the kids — Nudge is the clear winner. The Telegram integration alone makes it dramatically easier to adopt than anything else on this list. Todoist remains king for individual productivity, and Cozi works for grandparents who just need a calendar. But for modern families who want their system to work for them (not the other way around), Nudge is the answer.

tips.tip: Most families try 2-3 apps before finding one that sticks. Start with a free trial of your top 2 choices.
Involve your kids in the decision. The app they help choose is the app they'll actually use.
Look for Telegram or WhatsApp integration — kids don't check separate apps, but they do check their messages.
